title: A specified finite free presentation yields a Hom kernel on the same open
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], G and F arbitrary O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], V an open of X and m,n >= 0. Suppose a: O_V^{oplus m} -> O_V^{oplus n} is a module morphism on the slice site over V, with a specified isomorphism e: Coker(a) ~= G|_V [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. Then there is a morphism alpha: (F|_V)^{oplus n} -> (F|_V)^{oplus m} of O_V-modules whose kernel is isomorphic to Hom_O_X(G,F)|_V [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. The conclusion uses scheme restriction along V -> X on precisely that same open V and the same ranks; neither G nor F is required to be coherent.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01CO (1), Lemma 01CQ, and proof of Lemma 01CP; Sites, Modules, Lemma 0E8H.

proof.text: On the slice site over V let R = X.sheaf.over V, M = F.over V, and H = (homFunctor R).flip.obj M. Install the symmetric monoidal closed structures and compare H with MonoidalClosed.internalHom.flip.obj M using ihom_obj and pre_app. The latter preserves equalizers, and preservesLimitsOfShape_of_natIso transfers this property to H. Apply CokernelCofork.IsColimit.ofπOp to the specified cokernel cofork, then isLimitForkMapOfIsLimit' to H. The resulting limiting fork gives H(cokernel a) isomorphic to kernel(H.map a.op); H.mapIso e.op identifies its source with Hom(G.over V,F.over V).

Use the proved upstream Functor.opMapBiproductIso and SheafOfModules.homObjUnitIso to identify the Hom objects out of the finite sums of restricted units with the sums of M indexed by Fin n and Fin m. Define alpha = hn.inv followed by H.map a.op followed by hm.hom. The square commutes by hn.hom_inv_id_assoc. kernel.mapIso transports the preceding kernel isomorphism to kernel alpha. No conversion to ULift-indexed free modules or coordinate formulas is needed.

Use the proved upstream overHomObjIso to identify the source with (homObj G F).over V. Let T = (overEquiv V).functor. T.mapBiproduct and the components of overFunctorEquiv identify T of each sum of M with the corresponding sum of F.restrict V.ι. Conjugate T.map alpha by these isomorphisms to define beta. PreservesKernel.iso and kernel.mapIso identify T(kernel alpha) with kernel beta. Compose with the inverse component of overFunctorEquiv at homObj G F to obtain the required scheme-restriction isomorphism. All constructions remain valid for m = 0, n = 0, and V empty.

lean.statement:
theorem homObj_locally_kernel_of_local_presentation
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (G F : X.Modules) (V : X.Opens) (m n : ℕ)
    (a : (⨁ fun _ : Fin m ↦ (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).over V) ⟶
      (⨁ fun _ : Fin n ↦ (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).over V))
    (e : (cokernel a) ≅ G.over V) :
    ∃ (α : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n ↦ F.restrict V.ι) ⟶
      (⨁ fun _ : Fin m ↦ F.restrict V.ι)),
      Nonempty ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
        (SheafOfModules.homObj (R := X.sheaf) G F) ≅ kernel α)
